Trunks and divisions of the Russian soil classification (internal)

Source: R/diagnostics-kidpr.R
kidpr2008_divisions.Rd

The predicates of the keys to trunks and divisions of the Russian soil classification (Field Guide of 2008, keys 2.2 and 2.3), read by classify_kidpr2008 through the flattened key of inst/rules/kidpr2008/key.yaml and divisions/. They read the identified horizons of the profile (identify_horizons: the Russian notation where the profile is written in it, else key 2.1 on the data) and a few site facts. Each returns a DiagnosticResult: TRUE, FALSE, or NA when an undecided layer or a missing record (a depth among them) could change the answer.

Usage

has_horizon_kidpr(pedon, codes, within_cm = NULL, buried = FALSE)

starts_at_surface_kidpr(pedon, codes, from_ground_zero = FALSE)

surface_horizon_kidpr(pedon, codes)

directly_over_kidpr(pedon, upper, lower, gap_cm = 0)

below_kidpr(pedon, upper, lower)

only_horizons_kidpr(pedon, sets, raw = FALSE)

rock_within_kidpr(pedon, max_cm = 30)

turbated_kidpr(pedon, min_cm = 40)

peat_body_kidpr(pedon, min_cm = 50)

surface_deposit_kidpr(pedon, min_cm = 40, humified = NULL)

stratified_body_kidpr(pedon, min_cm = 40)

soil_horizon_within_kidpr(pedon, max_cm = 100)

floodplain_kidpr(pedon)

volcanic_ash_kidpr(pedon)

contaminated_x_kidpr(pedon, within_cm = 30)

Arguments

pedon

A PedonRecord.

codes, upper, lower

Russian horizon codes ("BT", "G" ...).

within_cm

A layer starting less than this depth below the ground (NULL: any depth); a layer of unknown depth leaves it undecided.

buried

Also read the horizons of buried soils.

from_ground_zero

For starts_at_surface_kidpr: a TRUE answer stands only when the description starts at 0 cm (fresh litter included), else it is undecided (a truncated soil, Hugo's decision Q19).

gap_cm

Thickness of layers with no diagnostic horizon allowed between upper and lower.

sets

A list of code vectors: the profile's horizons must be exactly one of them.

raw

For only_horizons_kidpr: read every horizon of the profile, before the thickest-horizon rule of the surface.

max_cm, min_cm

Depth or thickness limits (see each predicate).

humified

For surface_deposit_kidpr: TRUE a deposit with RJ, RY or RU, FALSE one without, NULL either.

Value

A DiagnosticResult.

Details

The profile is read top-down from the ground. A deposit at the surface (surface_deposit_kidpr) is the run of technogenic formations (TPO), deposits (horizon key position 38b), stratified humus horizons (RJ, RY, RU), small deposited layers (r, rh, ur, rr, rx) and loose rock over a buried soil or an organic or humus horizon; under a deposit of 40 cm or less the soil below is the one keyed. Sub-horizons are merged, small horizons and transitions left out (the FAO and WRB transitions AB, BC, E/B ... too, when the key on the data finds no diagnostic horizon in them); of the organic, humus and agro horizons that start the profile the agro horizon is kept and, of the natural ones, the thickest (the others are features; a W of 5 cm or less over another horizon is the feature w).

has_horizon_kidpr

One of the horizons is in the profile (an overlay S or X counts; a V laid over another horizon is a feature of its layer).

starts_at_surface_kidpr

The first horizon of the profile (at the surface, or under a deposit of 40 cm or less) is one of the horizons.

surface_horizon_kidpr

The surface horizon (the agro horizon, else the thickest natural organic or humus horizon that starts the profile) is one of the horizons.

directly_over_kidpr

One of the upper horizons lies directly over one of the lower ones (transitions and small horizons between them do not count; layers with no diagnostic horizon up to gap_cm thick are passed over).

below_kidpr

One of the lower horizons lies somewhere below one of the upper ones.

only_horizons_kidpr

The horizons of the profile (rock and parent material left out), read after the thickest-horizon rule, are exactly one of the sets; with raw = TRUE read before it.

rock_within_kidpr

Hard rock (R) starts within max_cm of the soil surface, organic horizons included (key C.1).

turbated_kidpr

A turbated horizon TUR more than min_cm thick (Hugo's decision Q20).

peat_body_kidpr

A peat body of more than min_cm: the organic layers contiguous from the surface (or under a deposit of 40 cm or less), muck and the agro-peat horizons included (key 2.2, step 6; Hugo's decision Q22); a layer the data leave undecided between peat horizons counts. A description that ends in peat short of it leaves it undecided.

surface_deposit_kidpr

A deposit at the surface (key 2.2, steps 2-4; Hugo's decision Q21) more than min_cm thick, with (humified = TRUE) or without (FALSE) a stratified humus horizon RJ, RY or RU.

stratified_body_kidpr

A stratified humus body from the surface, the agro horizons P and PU over RJ, RY or RU counted with them, of min_cm or more (the stratozems, B.2; Q21).

soil_horizon_within_kidpr

A soil horizon (of the profile or of a buried soil) starts within max_cm of the ground (key 2.2, step 1). A layer the data leave undecided between soil horizons is one; a layer in which the key on the data finds no diagnostic horizon (position 66) proves nothing, since it may be a transition; only rock, TPO and the deposit of position 38b rule a soil horizon out.

floodplain_kidpr

The soil lies within a river floodplain on modern alluvium (B.1; Hugo's decision Q21): a floodplain recorded (landform or landform element; a terrace is none) and alluvial material (the alluvial mark of the notation, or a fluvial or lacustrine origin of a layer or of the parent material; marine and glaciofluvial material and outwash do not count); with no landform recorded, alluvial material that soilKey's fluvic material confirms; alluvial material alone leaves it undecided. Nothing recorded: not a floodplain soil.

volcanic_ash_kidpr

The soil is developed in volcanic ash: the ash mark of the notation, an ash, tephra or pyroclastic origin of a layer or of the parent material, or 30 no ash. The key does not read it: the ochre horizon BAN is formed in ash by its definition, so BAN alone makes the volcanic soils (Hugo's decision of 2026-11-02).

contaminated_x_kidpr

The chemically contaminated horizon X in a layer starting within within_cm (C.3; Hugo's decision Q23): an X of the profile, or pollutants of the extremely hazardous category (contamination_hazard); contamination recorded without its category (site$contaminated, contamination_type) leaves it undecided; nothing recorded, no X.
